info.desc: Urban Hymns is the third album by English rock band The Verve, released on 29 September 1997. It earned nearly unanimous critical praise upon its release and went on to become the band's best-selling release and one of the biggest-selling albums of the year. The album received nearly unanimous critical praise upon its release, with Melody Maker naming Urban Hymns as the number-one album of 1997 in its year-end list. The album is featured in the book "1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die". In the years following its release, Urban Hymns received much acclaim. In 1998, it won .

podcast.body: The Verve's 1997 album "Urban Hymns" showcases Pete Salisbury's distinctive drumming style. On this album, Salisbury avoids simple 4/4 beats, instead laying down intricate and "out of the box rhythms" with a notable interplay between his left hand on the snare and right foot on the bass drum, utilizing a 4-piece kit and the matched grip. "To illustrate what I'm talking about, I want to play you a song from the Verve's 1997 album Urban Hymns."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: History of the Modern Drum Kit

podcast.body: The Verve's entire third album was recorded in Studio One at Olympic Studios. "The Verbs entire third album was made there in Studio One."

podcast.body: The album featuring "Bittersweet Symphony" became a global sensation. However, due to a complex sampling dispute, all songwriting credits for "Bittersweet Symphony" were signed over to Allan Klein, who then credited Mick Jagger and Keith Richards, preventing The Verve or Richard Ashcroft from earning royalties from the song for over 20 years. "who then slapped the names Jagger Richards on all the copies of the song and the album Urban Hymns."

podcast.body: This album was intended to make 1997 a great year for the band, featuring their brilliant song "Bitter Sweet Symphony." "1997 was supposed to have been a great year for the band thanks to their brilliant urban hymns album."

podcast.body: This album, released in 1997, became a significant hit for The Verve, with the song "Bittersweet Symphony" placed at its beginning. "They slapped it at the beginning of their 1997 album Urban Hymns and they saw it become a big hit, the biggest of their career actually."
